title: fix(core): make mustReply throw when the replied message is missing
body:
> **AI disclosure:** an AI coding agent (Claude Code, by Anthropic) wrote this fix and its tests, and ran the checks below. @OxFrancesco asked for it to be submitted.

Closes #185.

`mustReply: true` is supposed to throw `MtMessageNotFoundError` when the message being replied to doesn't exist. It never did. `getMessages` returns `(Message | null)[]`, so `msg` was `[null]` and `!msg` was always false. The send went through, and Telegram posted it as an ordinary message. The fix destructures the first element, as the other single-message `getMessages` call sites already do.

## Tests

Two cases added to `send-text.test.ts` under `describe('mustReply')`:

- `getMessages` answers with `messageEmpty`: `sendText` must reject with `MtMessageNotFoundError`, and `messages.sendMessage` must not be called.
- `getMessages` answers with the message: the reply is sent with `inputReplyToMessage` / `replyToMsgId: 42`.

## Reproduce

Without an account, run the new test against the old line:

```sh
git checkout master -- packages/core/src/highlevel/methods/messages/send-common.ts
pnpm exec vitest --config .config/vite.ts run packages/core/src/highlevel/methods/messages/send-text.test.ts
# × should throw and not send when the message does not exist
# AssertionError: expected error to be instance of MtMessageNotFoundError
# Tests  1 failed | 11 passed (12)

git checkout HEAD -- packages/core/src/highlevel/methods/messages/send-common.ts
pnpm exec vitest --config .config/vite.ts run packages/core/src/highlevel/methods/messages/send-text.test.ts
# Tests  12 passed (12)
```

With a real account, the script in #185 sends to Saved Messages with `replyTo: 2_000_000_000, mustReply: true`. On 0.30.3 it posts the message and returns no reply header, where it should throw.

## Checks

Run in Docker (`node:24-bookworm-slim`, pnpm 10.34.4, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `gen-tl`), with tests run under `--network none`:

- `pnpm test`: 154 files passed, 11 skipped; 1340 tests passed, 4 skipped
- `pnpm exec eslint` on both changed files: clean
- `pnpm lint:tsc`: exit 0

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(bun): truncate the file downloadToFile writes to
body:
Fixes #183

Bun's `FileSink` writes from the start of the file without truncating it, so `downloadToFile` over an existing, longer file left the old file's tail after the download. The file is now emptied with `Bun.write(filename, new Uint8Array(0))` before the writer is opened, matching what the Node and Deno versions already do.

## Test
A case in `packages/bun/src/methods/download-file.test.ts`: download 5 bytes over an existing 100-byte file and expect exactly those 5 bytes.
- without the fix: fails with `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 7, …(94)]`
- with the fix: passes, along with the two existing cases

I ran it with `bun --bun node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs --config .config/vite.ts run packages/bun/src/methods/download-file.test.ts`. On my machine `pnpm run test:bun` ran the workers under Node and skipped the Bun-only tests.

---

title: fix(core): set forumTopic flag for private threaded chats in send-text
body:
Fixes the leftover from #153, flagged there as a "separate issue" in [comment 4984437183](https://github.com/mtcute/mtcute/issues/153#issuecomment-4984437183).

## Problem

For a bot in a private chat with "threaded mode" enabled, `sendText` with `threadId` correctly delivers the message to the topic, but the returned `Message` has `isTopicMessage === undefined`:

```ts
const topic = await tg.createForumTopic({ chatId: USER_ID, title: "T" });
const threadId = topic.replyToMessage!.threadId!;
const sent = await tg.sendText(USER_ID, "probe", { threadId });
console.log(sent.isTopicMessage); // undefined
```

The message IS delivered to the topic (verified from the user side: incoming updates carry `forumTopic: true`), but the `Message` synthesized from `updateShortSentMessage` lacks the flag. This makes delivery look like "landed in General" unless you verify from the other side — which is exactly what tripped the original #153 report.

## Cause

ef4395d ("properly handle replyTo in send-text") reconstructs the reply header but derives `forumTopic` only for forum **channels** (`peerChannel` + `chat.forum`). Private chats (`peerUser`) are excluded.

## Fix

For `peerUser` chats, set the flag when `replyToTopId` is present (and ≠ 1). This is safe against over-flagging: the synthesized header is built from the input (`_inputReplyToToHeader`), and `inputReplyToMessage.topMsgId` is only populated from `params.threadId` — a plain reply (`replyTo` without `threadId`) never produces `replyToTopId`, so it won't be flagged.

Semantics note: with `threadId` set to a bot-space ID (invalid topic ID, see #153), the flag is now `true` even though the server routes the message to General. The flag reflects the sender's targeting intent (the request did target a thread); server-side routing of an invalid ID is a separate concern documented in #153.

## Verification

- Unit tests added (forum-channel flag preserved, private threaded flag set, plain reply not flagged).
- Live-tested against real Telegram (mtcute 0.32.4, layer 229, bot + userbot in a private threaded chat): `isTopicMessage` is `true` for `threadId` sends, `undefined`/`false` for plain `replyTo` — matching the server-side view from the userbot.

title: fix(core): pass disableWebPreview and geo accuracy to telegram
body:
two options mtcute accepted but never sent to telegram:

- `BotInlineMessage.text(..., { disableWebPreview: true })` did nothing. `_convertToTl` built the `inputBotInlineMessageText` without `noWebpage`, so links always got a preview. this affects `answerInlineQuery` and `answerBotGuestChatQuery`
- `accuracy` on `geo` / `geo_live` (documented as "estimated horizontal accuracy, in meters") was never mapped to `inputGeoPoint.accuracyRadius`. that's true for inline messages and for `sendMedia` (`_normalizeInputMedia`)

the other `inputBotInlineMessage*` constructors already map every field. inline results don't have an `accuracy` option, so they're unchanged

the regression tests for both fail without the fix. also tested live with a bot, stock 0.32.4 vs this branch:

| | 0.32.4 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| guest chat answer, link + `disableWebPreview` | preview shown | no preview |
| guest chat answer, `geo` / `geo_live` with `accuracy: 50` | not set | `accuracy_radius: 50` |
| `sendMedia` `geo` / `geo_live` with `accuracy: 50` | not set | `accuracyRadius: 50` |

title: fix(core): fall back to other dc addresses when connecting fails
body:
Closes #177

Covers the main ask of the issue (falling back to other addresses, incl. the built-in ones). The other two suggestions, a `dcOverrides` option and bounded request timeouts, are not part of this PR.

## Problem

Each DC connection used a single address, `ConfigManager.findOption()` → `options[0]`, and reconnected to it forever. On networks that block that address's range (e.g. `91.108.56.0/22`, which holds dc 5's only config IPv4), every request to that dc hung forever.

## Changes

- `ConfigManager.findOptions()`: all matching options, preference-ordered (stable). `findOption()` = first of these.
- Built-in production dc list (same as tdesktop `kBuiltInDcs` / tdlib `ConnectionCreator`), used as a fallback after the config's addresses, and for the primary dc (restored from storage) too. Only enabled (`NetworkManagerParams.builtinDcFallbacks`) when the client has no custom `defaultDcs` and isn't in test mode, so clients on other networks never get connected to Telegram (which could end in a `-404` → re-auth and an overwritten stored key). IPv6 only with `useIpv6`.
- `PersistentConnectionParams.dcFallbacks`: on connect failure, switch to the next address (wrap around, stay on the one that works). The codec is recreated because MTProxy and auth depend on dc id and the media flag.
- `PersistentConnectionParams.dcFailures`: a per-dc map of addresses that failed in the last 10 min, shared by every connection of a `DcConnectionManager`. Connections skip those addresses, so each new connection doesn't pay the timeout again. Only failures are shared, not "last working address", so on a healthy network media connections don't get pulled off media-only addresses.
- Address keys (`getDcOptionAddressKey`) normalize IPv6 via `ip.prettify`, so expanded/compressed notations dedupe and share failure state.
- Connect timeout, only when fallbacks exist (otherwise we'd retry the same address anyway): 15s, doubled after every failed round over all addresses, max 60s, so slow proxied connects still get through. The outer abort signal is forwarded manually (no `AbortSignal.any` on this path). The timeout is logged at warn when switching and not passed to `handleError`/`emitError`. Other connect errors are reported as before.
- After a full round of failed connects over all of a connection's addresses, one `MtcuteError` ("Could not connect to DC N using any of its addresses (…)") is emitted via `onError`, so a fully unreachable dc is still visible to the client error handler. It's counted per connection (consecutive failures % address count), not per dc. For a dc without an auth key only the main connection connects anyway.
- Read and ping timeouts (`_checkTimeouts`) are only checked while the socket is open. While connecting, a connection that already had an auth key would reset the session every ~7s. The old session's messages stayed queued and were sent after connecting, which produced `invalid sessionId` warnings.
- `_authorize()` defers to `onConnected()` if the socket isn't open yet (it only starts connecting). `requestAuth()` from `_getOtherDc` used to start the handshake before the socket existed, so its 5s timeout ran during the connect and failed on any connect slower than 5s.
- Failed auth attempts drop their queued unencrypted messages, so a stale `req_pq` isn't sent on the new socket (it caused a nonce mismatch and an extra reconnect).
- `changeTransport` now goes through the connect wrapper (it previously bypassed flood control), and fuman always gets the same address object (it checks identity).

## Deliberate limits

- No built-in addresses with custom `defaultDcs` (primary or secondary).
- `getDcOptionAddressKey`, `dedupeDcOptions`, `builtinProductionDcs` are exported from `utils/dcs.ts`, so they become public via `@mtcute/core/utils.js`. Happy to make them internal.
- Only TCP connect failures trigger a switch.
- Connections that start at the same time still wait for the first timeout together (once).

## Testing

- unit:
  - `config-manager.test.ts`: `findOptions`
  - `persistent-connection.test.ts`: rotation, wrap-around, timeout, no timeout without fallbacks, shared failures, failure TTL, timeout not reported, timeout escalation, "all addresses failed" reported once per round, queue purge
  - `session-connection.test.ts`: read timeout only while connected, no handshake before the socket is open
  - `network-manager.test.ts`: built-in fallbacks for the primary dc, none with custom `defaultDcs`. Existing tests now mock `findOptions` instead of `findOption`
  - `dcs.test.ts`: IPv6 key normalization, dedupe
  - `pnpm test packages/core`: 96 files, 798 passed, 2 skipped
- manual repro: block tcp to `91.108.56.0/22`, then `client.call({ _: 'help.getNearestDc' }, { dcId: 5 })` should resolve via `149.154.171.5` instead of hanging


---
